name_en: Damako nabe — pounded rice dumpling hot pot
summary_ja: 炊きたてのご飯をすりこぎで軽くつぶして丸めた「だまこ」を、比内地鶏の出汁でごぼうやせりと煮る鍋。八郎潟の魚が減り、代わりに鶏を使うようになったのが始まりと伝わる。
summary_en: Freshly cooked rice, lightly pounded with a pestle and rolled into balls called 'damako', simmers in hinai-jidori chicken broth with burdock and Japanese parsley — said to have taken shape once fish from Lake Hachirogata grew scarce and chicken took their place.
source_title: だまこ鍋 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Natto jiru — pureed fermented soybean miso soup
summary_ja: すり潰した納豆を溶き入れた味噌汁に、里芋やきのこ、山菜を加えた県南地域の郷土料理。納豆発祥の地の一つとされる横手市に伝わり、正月三が日に温め直して食べる習わしがあるという。
summary_en: Finely mashed fermented soybeans are stirred into a miso soup of taro, mushrooms, and wild greens — a dish tied to Yokote, one of the places said to claim natto's origin, traditionally reheated and eaten over the first three days of the New Year.
source_title: 納豆汁 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kiritanpo nabe — grilled rice-paste stick hot pot
summary_ja: 少し硬めに炊いたご飯を棒に付けて焼いた「たんぽ」を鍋の大きさに切り、比内地鶏の出汁でごぼうやせりと煮込む。炭焼きで山にこもる人々の残りご飯の食べ方が始まりと伝わる、大館・鹿角地方の郷土料理。
summary_en: Slightly firm rice is pressed onto a stick and grilled into 'tanpo', then cut to size and simmered in hinai-jidori chicken broth with burdock and parsley — said to have begun as a way charcoal makers used up leftover rice while holed up in the mountains.
source_title: きりたんぽ鍋 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Imonoko jiru — taro and chicken autumn soup
summary_ja: 里芋の子芋や孫芋「いものこ」を、鶏肉やきのこ、山菜とともに味噌や醤油で煮た秋の汁物。横手市山内地域特有の土壌で育つ里芋は柔らかな歯ごたえが特徴で、県北のきりたんぽ鍋と対比される郷土料理と伝わる。
summary_en: Baby taro corms called 'imonoko' simmer with chicken, mushrooms, and wild greens in miso or soy — an autumn soup said to use taro grown in Yokote's Sannai district, prized for its soft bite, and set alongside kiritanpo nabe as the region's autumn counterpart.
source_title: いものこ汁 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Junsai nabe — water shield hot pot
summary_ja: 沼で育つ水草じゅんさいのゼリー状の新芽を、鶏肉やごぼう、せりと煮た鍋料理。つるりとした喉ごしが持ち味で、日本有数の産地である三種町では箱舟で手摘みする夏の風物詩と伝わる。
summary_en: The jelly-coated young shoots of junsai, a water shield that grows in ponds, simmer with chicken, burdock, and Japanese parsley — prized for a smooth, slippery bite, and said to be hand-picked from small boats each summer in Mitane, one of Japan's leading junsai-growing towns.
source_title: じゅんさい鍋 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Tara jiru — whole cod miso soup
summary_ja: 真鱈を身からあら、肝、白子まで丸ごと使い、ねぎと味噌で仕立てた冬の汁物。にかほ市金浦山神社の鱈祭り「掛魚祭り」で振る舞われる、300年以上続く行事とともに伝わる秋田の冬の定番料理。
summary_en: Whole Pacific cod — flesh, bones, liver, and milt — simmers with scallion in a miso broth, a winter staple said to be served at Nikaho's 300-year-old cod festival, 'kakeyo matsuri', at Konoura Yama Shrine.
source_title: 鱈汁 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Shottsuru nabe — sailfin sandfish hot pot in fish sauce broth
summary_ja: 秋田の魚醤しょっつるを昆布出汁に合わせ、ハタハタと豆腐、白菜などの野菜を煮る冬の鍋。発祥地の男鹿市ではハタハタだけのシンプルな汁で食べると伝わり、雷鳴とともに沿岸に群れる時季に食べられる。
summary_en: Shottsuru, Akita's fermented fish sauce, is blended into a kelp broth to simmer sailfin sandfish with tofu and napa cabbage — a winter hot pot said to be kept simplest, just fish and broth, in Oga, where it's said to have begun, timed to the fish's thunder-season run inshore.
source_title: しょっつる鍋 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kyanokko jiru — finely diced root vegetable miso soup (also keno jiru)
summary_ja: 大根や人参、さつまいも、山芋などをけんちん汁より細かく刻み、味噌仕立ての出汁で煮た小正月の行事食。別名けの汁。大鍋で作り置き、無病息災を願いながら数日かけて食べる風習と伝わる。
summary_en: Daikon, carrot, sweet potato, and mountain yam, diced even finer than for kenchin soup, simmer in a miso broth — a dish for Koshogatsu, the 'little' New Year, also called 'keno jiru', said to be made in a big pot and eaten over several days for good health.
source_title: きゃのっこ汁／けの汁 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
